Website design in Odessa, TX has to serve two readers at once. One is the company man or plant manager deciding whether your outfit can handle the job. The other is the welder, driver or mechanic deciding whether your yard is a good place to work. In a city built on hands-on field work, most small companies are selling and hiring in the same week, and their website should do both.

Maurice Johnson writes each site by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. You get a free demo first. If you go ahead, it is $497, $997 or $1,997, paid once.

A field town, on paper and on the road

The Odessa metro covers all of Ector County, and HUD's housing market analysis for Odessa describes a local economy closely linked to oil and gas since oil was found in the Permian Basin in the 1920s, growing and slowing as oil prices rise and fall. Around them sit the welding shops, hot shot haulers, machine shops, tire and truck repair bays, and the taquerias and breakfast spots that open early for crews.

You can read it along the main roads, where shop buildings and equipment yards sit a short drive from retail strips and clinics. The city counted 115,743 people in the Census Bureau's 2023 estimate, and 61.2% of residents are Hispanic or Latino, so plenty of customers and job seekers grew up switching between English and Spanish.

Two jobs, one website

Winning the work

  • A services page that names each job you do, written the way a buyer would search for it.
  • A coverage map or county list: Ector, Midland, Andrews, Winkler, Ward, wherever your trucks really go.
  • Your safety program and any training your crews hold, stated plainly and accurately.
  • A bid or quote request form that reaches your inbox, plus one-tap calling for the urgent ones.

Filling the trucks

  • A careers page with each open role, the license or experience it takes, and the schedule.
  • A short application form, so a driver can apply from a phone in a parking lot.
  • Photos of your actual yard, shop and equipment, which tell an applicant more than a paragraph.
  • A standing note for when you are not hiring, so good people can still reach you later.

Most website templates have no place for that second column. We build it in from the start, and changing the openings is part of routine updates.

Who is training the next hire

Odessa's schools feed the same workforce your careers page is trying to reach. Odessa College runs a Truck Driving Academy whose course of up to 200 hours prepares students to test for a Class A commercial driver's license, and in January 2023 the Permian Strategic Partnership announced $3.5 million for the academy to add trucks, instructors and scholarships, citing a regional shortage of CDL drivers. The University of Texas Permian Basin is here in Odessa as well. Listing the licenses and certificates you want, in the same words those programs use, helps their graduates find your openings.

Workforce Solutions Permian Basin, part of the statewide Texas Workforce Solutions network with the Texas Workforce Commission, has an Odessa office on JBS Parkway, and employers can post jobs on WorkInTexas.com and get recruiting help at no cost. Your own careers page is not a replacement for that, but it is where an applicant goes to decide whether you are worth calling.

Website design Odessa TX shops and clinics can rely on

Not every business in town drives a truck. A dental office, a vet clinic, a barber or a family restaurant needs fewer pages and clearer basics: hours, location, what it costs or how to ask, and a phone number that dials with one tap. Google ranks local results by relevance, distance and prominence, so a site that names your side of town and the services you really offer gives the search engine something accurate to match. The same idea applies to web design Odessa TX trades depend on: describe the real work in the real places.

Free and low-cost help in Ector County

  • Odessa Development CorporationThe city's economic development corporation offers job creation grants, capital investment grants and other incentives to businesses expanding in Odessa.
  • Odessa Chamber of CommerceLists small business and entrepreneur support among its core work, and its economic development department is funded through the ODC, according to the chamber. It has co-hosted the Governor's Small Business Summit in Odessa.
  • UTPB Small Business Development CenterPart of UTPB's College of Business, it helps owners start, expand and grow, including business plans and getting ready for financing, and its director speaks to the ODC once a month.

Common questions

What should a website for an Odessa oilfield service company include?

Start with what a buyer checks before calling: the services you actually perform, the equipment you run, the counties you cover, your safety program and how to request a bid. Then add a careers page, because many field companies need workers as badly as they need jobs. Photos of your own yard and trucks help more than stock pictures.

How much is web design in Odessa, TX?

Ours is $497 for Starter, $997 for Pro or $1,997 for Agency, paid one time, and you own the site. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep one of our AI agents. Other designers price by the hour or the project, so ask each one for a written first-year total before you compare.

Can my website take job applications?

Yes. The careers page lists open roles with what each one requires, such as a Class A CDL, welding experience or a clean driving record, and a short form sends each applicant to your email. When you are fully staffed, the openings come down and the page says how to send a resume for later.

Can you write my site in Spanish?

We do not claim Spanish copywriting. If many of your customers or applicants read Spanish first, plan for Spanish pages written or reviewed by a fluent speaker you trust, and tell Maurice when you ask for the demo so the site is built with room for them.

Do you have an office in Odessa?

No. Maurice Johnson builds every site remotely from Big Sandy in East Texas. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
